label: sequence starts with s: late original-phase steps and <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token is s (32% of such steps active, 22x lift; 94% of activation mass), at original-phase steps t>=3 and on the <DEL> step, and never at t<3 or during the copy phase (2 copy-phase activations out of 94k). The input token at the current step does not matter. Activation ramps up after t=3 (step 3 is weak, often near 0), peaks around steps 4-6, and drops somewhat at <DEL>. The strongest examples start with s s. Weak leftover activations show up when s is the second original token (e.g. b s ...), mostly at later steps. Predicate on dev: P 0.93, R 0.73, F1 0.82, mass recall 0.94; most misses and false positives are near-zero activations.

issues: Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.932, R 0.729, F1 0.818, mass recall 0.938.
Copy-phase claim holds: 2 of 94,057 dev activations are in the copy phase (recall_idx 3); none at t<3 or t>=10.

Step 3 is the main source of false positives: first_tok==s & t==3 has precision 0.71 and only 5% of the mass. The explanation already says step 3 is weak, often near 0. Dropping it (t>=4) raises precision to 0.996 but lowers F1 to 0.753, so including it is reasonable.
The <DEL> step holds 19% of the mass (first_tok==s & phase==1: precision 0.97). For L=3 the <DEL> step is mostly inactive (precision 0.43), but that is only 0.07% of the mass, which is noise.

The misses are weak, lower-quartile activations, mostly in sequences where s is the second token. That clause alone has precision 0.23 and 5% of the mass. Adding it (even restricted to t>=6) lowers F1 to 0.79, which matches the other agent's report. Activations with no s in the first two tokens carry under 1% of the mass.
The 'input token does not matter' claim holds: in_tok lift is flat at about 1x for all original tokens. The out_tok=s lift is just the <DEL> step outputting orig(0)=s.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
